# crosswork_golden_config_jobs (Resource)

This resource applies a Golden Configuration template to devices and keeps it applied.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "crosswork_golden_config_jobs" "example" {
  template_name      = crosswork_golden_config_templates.example.name
  template_config_id = crosswork_golden_config_templates.example.config_id
  vendor             = "Cisco Systems"
  product_series     = "Cisco XRv 9000 Series Virtual Routers"
  mop                = "Default Golden Config - Cisco"
  devices = {
    "build-router-1" = {}
    "build-router-2" = {
      variables = [{
        name  = "ntp_server"
        value = "10.2.2.2"
      }]
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `devices` (Attributes Map) The devices the template is applied to, by inventory id, each with its associated values. A device that leaves the map has the configuration removed (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--devices))
- `mop` (String) Name of the MOP that applies the template, for example `Default Golden Config - Cisco`
- `product_series` (String) Product series sent with the job
- `template_config_id` (Number) Integer id of the configuration of the template (`config_id` of the template resource).
- `template_name` (String) Name of the template to apply
- `vendor` (String) Vendor sent with the job, as the template has it

### Optional

- `batch_size` (Number) Number of devices the controller configures in parallel; the controller uses 1 when it is not set
- `deployment_timeout` (Number) Seconds to wait for each job to finish, counted from when the job starts. It only limits how long Terraform waits and is not part of the Crosswork configuration. When it passes the apply fails and the job keeps running on the controller; the next apply runs it again
  - Range: `10`-`86400`
  - Default value: `900`
- `error_budget` (Number) Number of failures the controller tolerates before it stops a job; unset behaves like 1
- `instance` (String) Select an instance of the provider configuration by its name. Leave it unset to use the default instance.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags of the jobs
- `trigger` (String) A value, such as a hash of the template and its global variables, that triggers applying the template again to all devices when it changes.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The id of the object

<a id="nestedatt--devices"></a>
### Nested Schema for `devices`

Optional:

- `variables` (Attributes List) Device level variables, which are preferred over the template and the global variables (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--devices--variables))

<a id="nestedatt--devices--variables"></a>
### Nested Schema for `devices.variables`

Required:

- `name` (String) Variable name

Optional:

- `type` (String) Type of the value
  - Choices: `STRING`, `JSON`
  - Default value: `STRING`
- `value` (String) Value; for the type `JSON` a JSON document
  - **Required**: exactly one of `value` and `value_wo` must be set.
- `value_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Value
  - **Required**: exactly one of `value` and `value_wo` must be set.
- `value_wo_version` (Number) Rotation trigger for `value_wo`. Increment this integer whenever the write-only value changes so Terraform sends the new value.
